doc.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998

title: Picking and choosing work at an older age
summary: Wilder says offers are fewer now and playing with the Smithsonian Orchestra demands more effort, but he can decline jobs he would not enjoy.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: How has the work scene changed for you, like in the last ten years? Do you pick and choose a little more than usual?

I think you’re almost right on that. I think I’m picked and chosen on occasion. I sometimes have the privilege of deciding what I want to do, but the offers are not that numerous now. And you know the other thing is I’m much older and I started out as a young player and some of the older fellows were moved out to make room for me, and so it’s the same thing now. It’s something you have to accept and understand. Because as you get older there are a lot of things that I find — like playing with the Smithsonian Orchestra — I do them but I don’t do them with the ease that I did when I was younger. It really calls for a lot more concentration and a lot more practice. So I accept that. But I still can’t complain because I still get a lot of nice things, and most of them, with regard to picking and choosing, I do decide if I’m not going to enjoy doing it I won’t do it. I’m too old to be hassled by what I have to do.
